classification: EXPLORATORY / DESCRIPTIVE screen -- no confirmatory label, no LCB95 gate, no training
authorized_by: PI, 2026-09-22: 'Yes, go with that design ... freeze, contract, and run the fixed-at-start CLOSEST_DEFENDS screen at n=64.' Fixed-at-episode-start (single computation right after env.reset(), before any action) explicitly chosen over a dynamic per-tick reassignment, to change exactly one variable relative to the sealed bridge (the pair-selection RULE) without also introducing untested mid-episode role-switching.
QUESTION: Does forcing DEFEND onto the two ACTIVE agents closest to their own flag at the first decision tick (state-dependent, fixed for the whole episode) preserve the sealed scaffold bridge's crossover pattern (Delta_A' > 0, Delta_B' > 0, I_B < 0), or does the specific PAIR CHOICE matter more than the compositional headcount (2A/2D) the bridge's own diagnostics (I_A ~ -0.09, I_B ~ -0.49) suggested was the load-bearing variable?

WHY_THIS_LEVER.the_sealed_bridge: SCAFFOLDED_A_CROSSOVER_BRIDGE_4V4 (commit ef5ee95f, sealed SCAFFOLDED_CROSSOVER_CONFIRMED): forced pair chosen by PAIRS[seed % 6] (seed-rotated, NOT state-dependent). Delta_A' +0.352 [+0.234,+0.461]; Delta_B' +0.359 [+0.250,+0.469]; I_A -0.094 [-0.203,+0.016]; I_B -0.492 [-0.594,-0.391].
WHY_THIS_LEVER.the_hypothesis_under_test: I_A ~ 0 / I_B << 0 is the signature of a HEADCOUNT effect (4 attackers -> 2), not a WHICH-TWO effect. If true, any reasonable fixed-pair rule should reproduce the same pattern. This screen tests that with a rule that could plausibly differ (closest-to-home) from pure seed rotation.
WHY_THIS_LEVER.prior_learned_attempts_at_something_like: ROLE and Assignment-v1 (pre-scaffold 4v4 repairs) both showed the same Delta_A-passes/Delta_B-fails signature (ROLE +0.203/-0.047, Assignment-v1 +0.125/-0.016) as every non-scaffold repair. Their own design records were not re-read for this screen; this experiment tests the ALLOCATION RULE in isolation on the frozen specialists, not a new learned mechanism.
WHY_THIS_LEVER.successor_architecture_this_derisks: greedy_role_allocator(N, k_D) -> role-conditioned PPO, with k_D(4)=2 evaluated here; k_D for other team sizes (e.g. 6v6's candidate 5A/1D) is a SEPARATE, later experiment on that team's own specialists and certified poles -- this spec authorizes 4v4 only.

arms.pi_A: native pi_A3 (identical arm and checkpoint to the sealed bridge)
arms.A_closest: pi_A3 + 2D: the k_D=2 ACTIVE agents (alive, not tagged, not carrying -- the audit's own eligibility convention) closest to own_flag_home by Euclidean distance, computed ONCE at the state immediately after env.reset() (before any action; 'the first decision tick'), have their resolved target forced to DEFEND's live-state target for the REST of the episode. Same mechanism as the sealed A' (experiments.probe_learned_composition.install_forced_defend_target, same sha256 pin); the ONLY difference from A' is the pair-selection rule.
arms.pi_B: native corrected pi_B3 (identical arm and checkpoint to the sealed bridge)

DESIGN.fixed_vs_dynamic: FIXED AT EPISODE START. Computed exactly once, immediately after env.reset(), never recomputed. A dynamic per-tick reassignment is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this spec (see NOT_AUTHORIZED) -- it would confound two changes (pair rule AND mid-episode role-switching) in one experiment.
DESIGN.tie_breaking: stable argsort ascending by distance; ties broken by lower agent index. Structural probe (2026-09-22, read-only, no episode stepped) found no near-ties in practice: across 20 sample seeds the gap between the 2nd- and 3rd-closest agent was never below 0.358 cells (median 1.359); contract C6 re-checks this on the actual 64 seeds used.
DESIGN.poles: A = OP6 + frozen overlay (min_alive_for_defender = 4); B = the certified B3-3 genome SDS2_B3_LOCKDEF10_2V1 -- NEVER canonical OP7. Both attested against the governing certification, identical to the sealed bridge.
DESIGN.episodes: 64 seeds x 2 poles x 3 arms = 384 full episodes, deterministic, PPO off. Fresh seeds, disjoint from every prior block.
DESIGN.n_rationale: exploratory/screening scale (64), matching this project's own precedent for 'does a mechanism replicate under a changed condition, before deciding whether to invest training' checks -- cheaper than the 128 used for an actual confirmatory bridge, since no confirmatory claim is made here.

ENDPOINTS.reported: Delta_A_closest = WR(A_closest,A) - WR(pi_B,A); Delta_B_closest = WR(pi_B,B) - WR(A_closest,B); I_A = WR(A_closest,A) - WR(pi_A,A); I_B = WR(A_closest,B) - WR(pi_A,B); native_Delta_A, native_Delta_B (descriptive, non-gating). Same bootstrap as the sealed bridge (paired percentile, 20000 resamples, alpha 0.05, rng seed 7) for point estimates and intervals, reported for information ONLY.
ENDPOINTS.no_gate: NO LCB95 threshold is applied and NO terminal pass/fail label is produced. This is explicitly descriptive per the PI: 'descriptive comparison to the sealed bridge, no new confirmatory label.'
ENDPOINTS.pattern_match_rule: Delta_A_closest_mean > 0 AND Delta_B_closest_mean > 0 AND I_B_mean < 0 -- the sealed bridge's own defining pattern, evaluated on POINT ESTIMATES only, frozen before any data is read, reported as a single descriptive boolean alongside the raw numbers and the sealed bridge's own reference values (read programmatically from the sealed RESULT.json at analyze time, never hand-transcribed).
ENDPOINTS.also_reported: Blue goals and margin contrasts (descriptive); the distribution of pairs A_closest actually selected across the 64 seeds (diagnostic: is the selection meaningfully varied, or does it degenerate toward one or two pairs).

checkpoints.note: the same two checkpoints, by hash prefix, that the sealed corrected crossover evaluated (its log records sha 94dde69d091a... and 021342c84bbe...).

pole_attestation.rule: both poles are attested before any episode against the governing certification (fields and config hash), through experiments.pole_attestation, with the B3-3 genome file supplied so canonical OP7 can never be scored. Each episode additionally asserts the LIVE opponent batch and the live min_alive_for_defender equals 4, and fails closed otherwise. This is the defect that invalidated an earlier 4v4 experiment (a pi_B trained on canonical OP7 but scored on B3-3).

INTEGRITY_FROZEN.seed_registry: fresh exploratory block, disjoint from every sealed_confirmatory and exploratory block on record; contract C4 checks it is reserved before contracts pass.

CONTRACTS_BEFORE_ANY_SEED_IS_SPENT: C1 all pinned sealed inputs equal their pins
C3 both poles attested (Pole B = the B3-3 genome)
C4 seed block reserved / exploratory / unspent / disjoint
C5 closest_defends_pair matches an independent brute-force argsort recomputation exactly on 500 synthetic states (incl. inactive-agent exclusion and tie-breaking)
C6 spawn geometry is non-degenerate (2nd/3rd-closest gap > 1e-3 cells) on ALL 64 real seeds x 2 poles that will actually be used

C7 the harness (S._setup_poles / S._open_opponent / S.run_episode) reproduces a KNOWN sealed bridge row exactly for both native arms on both poles, proving this new runner's plumbing is wired correctly before trusting its own fresh cells
C8 A_closest is deterministic given (pole,seed) and demonstrably state-dependent (>= 2 distinct pairs across the first 4 seeds); policy parameter digests unchanged by any contract episode
C9 no seed-table side door: the source never calls pair_for_seed or indexes PAIRS[seed...]
C10 the descriptive pattern-match rule self-tests correctly on synthetic cases
C11 read-only fence: no training/optimizer call in the source
NOT_AUTHORIZED: PPO or any training; any change to pi_A, pi_B, the poles, the scaffold, or its sealed record
a dynamic / per-tick reassignment variant (explicitly deferred; would confound the pair-selection-rule test with an untested mid-episode role-switching phenomenon)
a 6v6 (or any other team-size) version of this screen -- k_D for other team sizes is a separate future experiment on that team's own specialists and certified poles
treating the descriptive pattern-match result as a confirmatory crossover claim, or applying any LCB95-based label to it
committing before contracts pass; reading any outcome while shards run; top-up; re-run
claim_boundary: Two frozen 4v4 learned specialists, the two certified 4v4 poles, fresh exploratory seeds, a rollout-time state-dependent-but-fixed defender assignment on pi_A only. A_closest is pi_A with an externally imposed, state-dependent defender assignment (closest-to-home at t=0), not a learned assignment. This is a DESCRIPTIVE screen, not a confirmatory claim: no LCB95 gate, no terminal pass/fail label. It answers whether the pair-selection RULE matters, not whether PPO can learn to select or execute it.
claim_ceiling: a descriptive statement about whether the closest-to-home pair rule reproduces the sealed bridge's own pattern of win-rate contrasts; nothing about learnability, PPO, pi_B, 6v6, or any other team size.
